annotationRationale: The method classifies power remainders by divisibility by five and uses a binomial expansion to prove that all nonconstant terms vanish modulo 125.
sourceMethod: Follows the first official solution, squaring nonmultiples of five and expanding the fiftieth power. Explicitly checks divisibility of the linear and quadratic terms.

review.mathCheck: Multiples of 5 give remainder 0. Otherwise N²=5m±1; in its 50th power, the first nonconstant terms have coefficients 250 and 30625, both divisible by 125, and all remaining terms contain 5³. Thus the only remainders are 0 and 1, both attained, giving B.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official AMC 10B #18's binomial approach, pp. 8 and 9. It explicitly verifies the low-degree terms that the official solution handles collectively.
review.annotationCheck: The modular-power conclusion is assessed, with the fully explained binomial expansion supporting it. All integer cases are covered without requiring Euler's theorem.
